item.title: Liangzhu, the coder 'village' at the heart of China's AI frenzy
item.description: Hangzhou, a suburb of China, is emerging as a new AI hub, attracting entrepreneurs and tech talent with its low rents and proximity to major tech companies. Supported by government subsidies and tax breaks, the city fosters a vibrant startup ecosystem where coders collaborate and innovate, particularly in AI.
item.dc:creator: Meaghan Tobin

item.title: Croatian right-wing singer, fans perform pro-Nazi salute at massive concert
item.description: A right-wing Croatian singer, Marko Perkovic, also known as Thompson, ignited controversy after performing a song featuring a pro-Nazi salute at a large concert in Zagreb. Meanwhile, in Turkiye, a 53-year-old man was seriously injured by a lion that escaped from a zoo in Manavgat. The escaped lion was later shot dead after the attack.

item.title: '100-year catastrophe': Nearly 80 killed in Texas flash floods - What we know so far
item.description: Devastating flash floods in Texas have resulted in at least 79 fatalities and numerous missing individuals, including children, during the Fourth of July holiday. President Trump declared it a "100-year catastrophe" and plans to visit the affected areas. Rescue efforts are intensifying as forecasters predict more heavy rain, with officials warning of a rising death toll across the flood-stricken state.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'It's ridiculous': Donald Trump mocks Elon Musk's 'America Party'; calls him a 'train wreck'
item.description: Donald Trump dismissed Elon Musk's newly launched "America Party" as "ridiculous," reaffirming his belief in the traditional two-party system. Trump's remarks followed Musk's unveiling of the party, intended to challenge the perceived "one-party system" in the United States. The Tesla CEO's move came after a public fallout with Trump over federal spending cuts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Israel strikes Houthi-linked ports in Yemen; targets include seized ship, power plant; IDF cites drone, missile threats
item.description: Early Monday, the Israeli military confirmed airstrikes on Houthi-linked sites across several Yemeni ports, including Hodeidah and Ras Issa. The IDF stated the strikes targeted locations used for attacks on Israel and threats to global shipping in the Red Sea. Key targets included the seized merchant ship 'Galaxy Leader' and the Ras Qantib power plant, allegedly used for military activities.

item.title: Pakistan's power struggle narrows to two men: Imran vs Munir
item.description: Pakistan's political arena is dominated by Army Chief Asim Munir, wielding influence across key institutions, and the imprisoned Imran Khan, who maintains strong public support. Khan has called for nationwide protests post-Muharram, challenging Munir's authority amidst rising public discontent. While Munir gains international recognition, Khan's movement thrives through a robust digital presence, potentially destabilizing the current power structure.
item.dc:creator: Omer Farooq Khan

item.title: ‘Worrying disappearance’: 18-year-old French national missing in Iran; 20 Europeans under detention in country
item.description: An 18-year-old Franco-German cyclist, Lennart Monterlos, has gone missing in Iran since June 16, prompting concern from French authorities. The disappearance occurs amidst warnings that Iran is deliberately targeting Westerners, particularly French nationals, on espionage charges. Several European nationals are currently detained in Iran, with accusations of spying for Israel, further escalating diplomatic tensions.

item.title: Latest Israeli strike kills 38 in Gaza: Israel, Hamas set for indirect talks; Qatar to mediate
item.description: Recent Israeli airstrikes in Gaza have resulted in the tragic loss of 38 Palestinian lives, according to hospital officials. The attacks, which targeted areas including Gaza City and Muwasi, come amidst renewed indirect negotiations between Israel and Hamas, mediated by Qatar. These talks aim for a ceasefire and hostage release, with the US proposing a 60-day truce.

item.title: ‘To spite Trump’: Laura Loomer predicts conservatives joining Musk's America Party; names 3 key figures
item.description: Laura Loomer predicts Tucker Carlson, Marjorie Taylor Greene, and Thomas Massie will join Elon Musk's America Party, potentially reshaping the conservative landscape. Loomer suggests Carlson's alignment with Musk offers an alternative to Trump, while Greene's anti-establishment views and Massie's fiscal conservatism align with the party's focus on budget cuts and freedom.

item.title: ‘Emergency situation’: Influx of Afghans returning to their country from Iran ahead of deadline; 250,000 already returned in June
item.description: Thousands of Afghans are returning from Iran due to an order. The UN reports an emergency at border crossings. Many Afghans are crossing into Herat province. A large number of returnees are children. The UN is providing aid like water and sanitation. The UN urges countries not to force Afghans to return. Afghanistan struggles with poverty and unemployment.

item.title: Thousands of UAE residents who invested in second passports fear visa bans as US, UK tighten CBI rules
item.description: Thousands of UAE residents who invested in Citizenship by Investment (CBI) programmes now face uncertainty as global mobility benefits come under scrutiny. With new US and EU regulations targeting weak CBI vetting, many expatriates fear losing visa-free access to key countries. Experts stress the need for reform, with alternatives like the UAE Golden Visa gaining popularity as more credible options.
